title: Sedona
dek: Six nights among the red rocks, built around a slow pace, a real spa day, and food that isn't the Uptown tourist strip — a first solo trip with room to breathe. Everything below is checked; tick items off as you go and your progress saves.
verified: Checked 19 Jul 2026 for the 2–8 Sep trip. Confirmed from primary sources: TSA REAL ID/passport rules (tsa.gov), the Red Rock Pass program and prices (fs.usda.gov, official Coconino National Forest), Sedona Shuttle's live route status (sedonashuttle.com — 2 of 3 free trailhead routes suspended), the Pocket Fire closure order and Oak Creek flooding closure (fs.usda.gov/r03/coconino/alerts, Forest Orders #03-04-00-26-004 and #03-04-06-26-002 — active through the trip window), Mii amo's current Journey package structure (miiamo.com — 2/3/4/7/10-night, not day treatments), Tlaquepaque's own hours (tlaq.com family of sources), local food picks cross-checked across multiple local guides, and Sedona/Cathedral Rock/Bell Rock/Airport Mesa/Tlaquepaque/Uptown/Phoenix coordinates (Nominatim). Time zone (America/Phoenix — Arizona observes no DST) resolved from Sedona's own coordinates via scripts/lookup-tz.mjs, not assumed from the country. The budget line was re-checked against its own numbers: the full week (including the Day 2 spa splurge) runs ≈$327/day, about 9% over the stated $150–300/day target, not just "approaching" it. ⚠ re-check before you go: exact hotel and rental-car rates (both move week to week), L'Auberge de Sedona's current spa-treatment prices (not published online — call to book), whether the Pocket Fire closure order (through Sep 30, unless rescinded early) or the Oak Creek flooding closure have lifted, the Sedona Shuttle's route status again close to your dates, and the NWS flash-flood/monsoon forecast in the days immediately before you go. Re-checked 23 Jul 2026: standard US tipping percentages/amounts (widely-cited convention, not a single official figure — treat the stated ranges as a starting point), Airport Mesa's upper-lot parking fee (multiple travel sources cite ≈$3, but no official Coconino National Forest or City of Sedona page names it directly, unlike the Red Rock Pass's confirmed $5/day — flagged, not dated), and Wildcraft Cafe's hours (aggregator listings show weekend hours differing from weekday, so the blanket "daily" claim was removed rather than left possibly wrong — confirm the day-of-week hours directly before relying on them).
footer: Location photos via Wikimedia Commons — tap any credit for its source, author and license.
intro: Six nights based in Sedona — a slow, single-base trip built around a spa day, real local food away from the Uptown strip, and the red rocks at an easy pace rather than a strenuous one. September falls squarely inside Arizona's monsoon season (mid-June through end of September) — afternoon thunderstorms and flash-flood risk are real considerations here, not a footnote, so outdoor time is planned for mornings. A rental car is the practical way to get around: rideshare coverage is inconsistent, and two of Sedona's three free trailhead shuttle routes are suspended for the Pocket Fire closures north of town (through Sep 30 — see Health & safety) — neither affects this trip's main hiking days, both south of the fire area.
